wsl-claude: yes, it does, and I should have said it plainly. Two options, and they differ exactly here:
A) NO CORE CHANGE: grantFace as an ordinary process job, started by hand in the jobs app. It runs, reports to the terminal, can be cancelled. But no autostart, no shutdown request, and it can outlive a killed node.
B) YOUR SCOPE, with autostart and autostop: a CORE change in three node files, spirit/run/js/jobs.js (server jobs get job id and door; the shutdown request), appServers.js (start an app's own server at boot) and server.js (ask the servers to stop when the node stops), plus one line in the jobs app (Cancel). kernel.js, the one every page and process loads, is NOT touched.
So 'no kernel change' was true; 'no core change' is only true for A. Autostart and autostop can't happen without the node itself doing them.

Not reliably. It depends on how the node dies and where:
- SPIRIT-3 UNDER SYSTEMD, normal stop or restart: yes. systemd stops the node's whole process group, children included.
- YOUR WINDOWS BOX, or ANY HARD KILL of the node alone: no. A process job is spawned with no tie to its node (jobs.js:203, no IPC line), and Windows does not end a child when its parent ends. It keeps running until it next tries to report to a door that's gone, and a job that never reports runs on.
Server jobs are different: they have the IPC line, so they exit the moment the node is gone, however it goes. That's the gap wsl-claude flagged, and it's why grantFace should run as a server, not a plain process.

wsl-claude: same answer as claude-windows, and the two facts behind it. 1) The node itself never stops its jobs: its stop path, goodbye(), tells open pages, closes the server and exits, with not a word to any job (server.js:2041-2050). 2) The systemd units don't set KillMode (bash/systemd/*.service), so systemd's default applies: stopping the unit kills its whole group, jobs included. That's why spirit-3 is clean and your Windows box isn't. So: under systemd, yes; anywhere else, only a server job's IPC line (or a job that fails its next report) ends it. That's the gap the shutdown request in your scope closes, everywhere.

Yes, B fits inside that line, with one piece left out. The process API as it stands is: the two environment variables (SPIRIT_JOB_ID, SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL), spirit.core.jobs.report/log/complete/fail, and the jobs.* verbs. B keeps all of them unchanged:
- A server gets the SAME two variables a process job gets. That's the existing contract, applied to one more kind of job.
- Autostart: the launcher reads a manifest field. That's the app's manifest, not the process API.
- Autostop: when the node stops, it closes each server's IPC line, the mechanism server jobs already exit on, and kills any still running after a few seconds. No message the process has to understand.
- Cancel for servers: the jobs app's own button; jobs.cancel already works on any kind.
LEFT OUT: the graceful shutdown request with a tidy-up hook (spirit.core.server.onShutdown). That WOULD be new process API, so it waits for its own item.
Go! = B on those terms.
